Review Title: Westwind Signature Grand Canyon Tour Exceeds Expectations
Review Text:
This was my anniversary gift for my wife and it exceeded every expectation. The staff, pilots and our tour guide on the ground (different company by Westwind coordinates for you) were all outstanding.

The plane seats 10 (I think). You need to be comfortable in a small plane with minor turbulence. The narration was very informative.

Make sure you order lunch beforehand. If you book through your hotel (like we did) make sure you tell them to order you lunch. Bring a lot of water. It isn’t a very physical tour but you will want to stay hydrated. If you go in the spring or fall don’t forget that it is noticeably cooler up at the Grand Canyon than it is in Phoenix. Review Title: Awe inspiring way to experience The Grand Canyon!
Review Text:
We had a once in a lifetime experience on Westwind's Signature Grand Canyon South and Ground Tour. I have a terrible fear of flying but I was desperate to be able to do this tour. If not today, when, was part of my logic.

My husband and I arrived at Sedona Airport and watched our plane arrive and I was happy to see the size of the plane. The captain came through the gate, introduced herself and asked if I was her guest! I told her I was and I was scared Sh**less:) Captain Carla was so kind and professional and assured me I would have a wonderful day and would be able to enjoy the flight. I was comforted by her kindness and assurances.

Upon boarding the plane with 8 wide comfortable seats for guests I knew if I sat and buckled up I would not turn back:) I did it!

The flight to the Grand Canyon was extremely calm and I found the guide information and soothing background music of the headset extremely calming! Captain Carla interupped the voice tour multiple times to point out various additional points of initerest! Captain even checked on how I was doing mid flight which was so kind!

The first view of the Grand Canyon in the distance is awesome! As we flew around the Canyon, the pictures and videos do not do it justice of the awe you feel viewing it from above! I am so very thankful I was able to complete the tour and feel I was able to do it because of Captain Carla. The Carla Touch:)

We were transferred to BuckWild Hummer Tour for the ground portion. I will review them on their page as well. Tom was our driver, the hummer was exceptionally comfortable, we traveled with a total of 12 guests. The rows of seats are stepped so the view from each row was great, not effected at all by persons in front of you! Great set up. Tom our driver was professional, and extremely knowledgable of all things related to The Grand Canyon park. It was a pleasure to get to know him during our 3 hour tour. He obviously loves his job and shares that feeling with his guests!

Our return flight to Sedona was a not as calm as outgoing but Captain Carla tried to find some smoother air but it was impossible. Even with the slight occassional bumps the flight was awesome, the views are just indescribable!

Thank you to Lindsey for arranging our reservation with kindness, and professionalism. Thank you to Captain Carla, without her calming, professionalism and expertise I don't know if I could have done it. Thank you to Tom for sharing his knowledge with us and his insights to The Grand Canyon as well as his wife who arranged all the lunches for our gourp!

I wish I could give this tour higher than a 5*!

Review Text:
I hate to write a review in the midst of COVID for a small business, but unfortunately due to our experience I’m writing this in hopes that nobody else has the same experience. We booked a PRIVATE Grand Canyon tour. We spoke with someone over the phone on multiple occasions who explained it would be just us with the possibility of one other person (although they explained that wouldn’t be likely). When it came time for our flight, the pilot + others arrived 20 minutes late, not wearing masks and informed us there would a total of 10 of us on the tour. As you can imagine, we were pretty surprised given that wasn’t what we signed up or paid for. The pilot explained something happened with scheduling and to call Lindsey. We did so and she provided pretty awful customer service. In short she explained yes there were gonna be 10 people and if we didn’t want to go we didn’t have to but either way we weren’t getting a refund or rescheduled.

Throughout the flight NOBODY including the guests or pilot wore a mask. Nobody suggested or asked for this to be done. This is unlawful in the state of Arizona and county of Sedona. Not only is this against the law, but put customers in great risk. I cannot believe they would allow this and be okay with this.

I am so disappointed in the service. Highly recommend researching other options prior to booking with this company. I am sure there are other much better companies that would provide honest and safe services.

Review Title: Misleading, overpriced and poor customer service
Review Text:

When we reached out thinking there was confusion we were told they got booked on her day off. Keep in mind this is in the midst of Covid so flying on a plane with 7 strangers who NONE INCLUDING THE PILOT WERE WEARING MASKS is not ideal.

We were told we did not purchase the cancellation insurance which was never presented when I booked over the phone and we could only get 50% refunded.

Review Title: Great way to see the Grand Canyon with limited time
Review Text: We stayed in Scottsdale for our vacation and took Westwind from the Deer Valley airport only 20 minutes away. Our family of five (kids 13, 10, 3) had never seen the Grand Canyon. Flying up there in 1 hour was such a treat over driving for 3.5 hours. Our two older kids really listened to the narrated history on the headphones the whole way up, and even our three year old looked out the window as we started to fly over the Grand Canyon itself. The view is absolutely stunning, and the flight was very smooth. Once we landed, the Pink Jeep tour guide did a great job telling us the history and getting us to each view point quickly and efficiently. They also added an Imax movie viewing of the Grand Canyon river tour as an added surprise, which all of us enjoyed. On the way back, our pilot Jameson had my 10 year old in the front as co-pilot, and he LOVED hearing all about the airplane and the landscape below the whole way back. The whole day was a great experience.

Review Title: Flight from Hell over the Grand Canyon...
Review Text:
I'm conflicted as to how to review Westwind as we had two different planes for our group of 16 family and friends (ages ranging from 25 - 60) who had completely different experiences on our flight over the Grand Canyon from Page Airport. My flight (which I'll refer to as plane 1), which was supposedly the NON-executive plane, had an awesome pilot named Mark, who communicated with us throughout the flight, pointing out where to look (and there's a lot you won't see/notice if you're not directed) and forewarning us of turbulence. His humor and constant, clear communication made a semi-scary extremely turbulent flight as comfortable as it could possibly be. A few of us threw up from the bumpiness, but we felt very safe in Mark's hands and were all happy with our experience.

Our other plane of 8 people however (plane 2), had an entirely different experience. This plane we were told was the "executive plane" - nicer seats, etc. However, unlike plane 1 which had secure shoulder straps and individual seats for each person, this plane only had waist belts, the last row of the plane was a bench, and their seats were not in a fixed position and so were aggressively sliding back and forth throughout the flight. This constant movement, paired with turbulence, resulted in everyone slamming their heads into the ceiling multiple times (confirmed by every passenger) and 5 of the 8 passengers vomiting throughout the flight (so much vomit that my mom (the guest of honor) had to clean out the plane after they landed while the pilot stood by watching). One person got so sick they had to go to the hospital afterwards and 3 others were ill for the rest of the day and unable to participate in the activities we had planned. Of the 8 people on plane 2, only TWO people actually saw the Grand Canyon because the others were so sick, or scared that they couldn't look.

To make matters worse, their captain, unlike ours, did not speak once throughout the entire flight. Not only did this mean they weren't getting told where to look (which you think would be a no-brainer for a tour like this), but it also made everyone incredibly nervous as they continued to hit worse and worse turbulence. Honestly, when I initially heard how terrible a time they had, I thought they were being dramatic, but when I heard THESE details (seats sliding around, heads slamming into the ceiling, and a captain who did not speak the entire 1.5 hour flight) and they were confirmed by every single passenger, I was furious.

Upon landing, as the majority of our group was throwing up outside the airport, the captains told us that that was the worst conditions they've ever flown through and that they were cancelling the rest of the flights for that day. While I'm of course glad that I (and the lucky others on plane 1 were able to see the Grand Canyon, I'm also a little skeptical of Westwind's judgment to 1) fly us in such bad conditions and 2) fly half of our group on a plane that seems incredibly unsafe and with a pilot who apparently doesn't have basic communication skills. That's not just "bad conditions," that is bad judgement and completely unacceptable and infuriating when lifes are on the line. And finally, it's really disappointing that a once in a lifetime experience was turned into a harrowing, sickening flight from hell.
